builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: When uncertainty quantification fails: structural vulnerabilities and corrections for selective prediction under clinical class imbalance
summary: The method replaces standard entropy-based uncertainty scoring and global coverage-risk selection with threshold-aligned uncertainty measures (e.g., distance to the decision boundary) plus class-stratified risk control. The cost is negligible computationally: it is a scoring and calibration change with no extra model training, inference overhead, or infrastructure. It can fail if the base classifier is poorly calibrated overall, if a usable decision threshold cannot be defined, or in regimes so extreme that no uncertainty measure can recover clinically meaningful ranking for the minority class.
rationale: It is a zero-infrastructure, post-hoc correction to uncertainty scoring and evaluation that directly fixes a documented failure mode relevant to any imbalanced classification pipeline in production.
technique: Threshold-aware uncertainty for selective prediction under class imbalance

claims.statement: The method replaces standard entropy-based uncertainty scoring and global coverage-risk selection with threshold-aligned uncertainty measures (e.g., distance to the decision boundary) plus class-stratified risk control. The cost is negligible computationally: it is a scoring and calibration change with no extra model training, inference overhead, or infrastructure. It can fail if the base classifier is poorly calibrated overall, if a usable decision threshold cannot be defined, or in regimes so extreme that no uncertainty measure can recover clinically meaningful ranking for the minority class.

Across 56 synthetic conditions and three clinical cohorts, threshold-aware metrics combined with class-conditioned risk control maintained bounded, balanced risk, whereas standard entropy-based selection either collapsed minority-class sensitivity or protected the minority at the expense of majority patients.
